newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus ministry rejects Yeltsin's wish for merger.
newsitem.headline: Belarus ministry rejects Yeltsin's wish for merger.

text.p: The Belarussian foreign ministry on Thursday rejected the idea of a complete merger with Russia, an idea outlined by President Boris Yeltsin.

"We are not talking about creating a single state. So far I see no possibilities, objective and legal, to merge the states, to abolish the state called the Republic of Belarus," Deputy Foreign Minister Mikhail Khvostov told a news briefing.
Khvostov was reacting to a television interview on Wednesday in which Yeltsin said he favoured an ultimate merger of the two Slav states, both former Soviet republics.
"I think we will reach the point of being a single state," Yeltsin told state-controlled Russian Television.

Yeltsin and hardline Belarussian President Alexander Lukashenko, who committed their countries to close integration in April 1996, are due to sign a charter on May 23 following a union treaty signed last month.
Lukashenko has always stressed the need to keep Belarus independent and to form a union of two equal, sovereign states. Khvostov reiterated this position on Thursday.

"Yes, Yeltsin's statement is a serious statement of a person who is a head of state...It will be studied but I would like to say that under no circumstances will the statehood of Belarus be placed in doubt," Khvostov said.

The idea of forming a union has broad support in both countries but is opposed by nationalists in Belarus who accuse Moscow of pursuing an imperialistic course and trying to end the independence Minsk won after the Soviet Union collapsed in 1991.
Russian liberals also warn Yeltsin against any deal with Lukashenko, whose authoritarian rule and poor record on human rights have made him a pariah in the West.
